newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Brit Biotech targets 1st drug launch.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Brit Biotech targets 1st drug launch.

text.p: Britain's flagship biotech company British Biotech Plc said on Wednesday that it was on target to launch its first product in 1998.

The Oxford-based research group, which is best known for its novel anti-cancer pill Marimastat, said it would seek marketing approval in Europe for a new drug to treat acute pancreatitis in the first three months of 1997.
Clinical trials of Lexipafant, which is to be sold under the name Zacutex, showed that the drug helped to combat the liver and kidney failure induced by acute pancreatitis.

There is currently little on the market to treat the condition, which kills up to 10 percent of all sufferers. Some 100,000 people in western Europe and 200,000 in the U.S. suffer from acute pancreatitis each year.

The announcement overshadowed second-quarter results, which showed losses widening to 8.1 million stg ($13.6 million) from 4.0 million as spending on the maturing drug pipeline climbs. Shares in the volatile stock rose 3 1/2 pence to 225 pence on the trial news in late morning trading, although analysts were reserving their judgement pending a meeting with the company.
Lehman Brothers analyst Ian Smith said details on just how effective the drug is would have an impact on how much the company could charge.

The market appeared to shrug off widely-expected news that British Biotech had dropped development of another anti-cancer drug, Batimastat, on the grounds that the injectable drug offered no advantages over the easier-to-take Marimastat.

However, some analysts expressed concern over the fate of another compound, which is being developed to combat side effects linked to chemotherapy, after British Biotech said results of the first of a series of intermediate-stage trials were "not encouraging."

Although it accounts for well under 10 percent of most analysts' valuations of the company, finance director James Noble said the news on Zacutex was "incredibly important. It changes us from a company that has a pipeline of ideas to one that should have a product on the market by 1998."

Noble said he was "comfortable" with analysts' predictions that sales of Zacutex would eventually reach $300 million if it gets to the market. He told Reuters that the company would probably ask regulators in the U.S, where trials are still underway, for approval early in 1998.
Shareholders will have to wait until May 1997 for more news on British Biotech's potential blockbuster drug Marimastat, which accounts for most of the share price valuation.

Noble said the company would probably use scientific meetings in May and November next year to give updates on progress of the drug, which is currently in Phase II and Phase III trials in a wide range of cancers. ($ = 0.595 British Pounds Sterling)
